findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed by changing letter case
findings.body: should_block? does an exact database string match on the supplied email, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator normalizes case (or surrounding whitespace) before lookup/storage. Email addresses are treated case-insensitively elsewhere (e.g. User.email_hash downcases), so a blocked address such as bad@spamclub.com can register as Bad@Spamclub.com and evade the block. Normalize emails to a canonical form (strip + downcase) on BlockedEmail save and in should_block? before querying.

findings.title: should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write and mutates state during validation
findings.body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator.validate_each, i.e. during model validation, yet it increments match_count/last_match_at with a non-atomic read-modify-write save. Two consequences: (1) concurrent registration attempts with the same blocked email lose increments (both read the same match_count and write the same +1 value) — use an atomic update such as update_all('match_count = match_count + 1'); (2) a single signup attempt validates twice (UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which re-validates), and attempts rejected for unrelated reasons also persist a count, so match_count does not reflect actual blocked attempts. The counter update should be atomic and ideally separated from the pure predicate.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is a mutable array defined on the controller prototype and shared by all instances
findings.body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined in the object passed to Discourse.Controller.extend, so the same array instance lives on the prototype and is shared across every instance of the controller rather than being per-instance state. pushObject in createAccount therefore leaks rejected addresses across controller instances / modal lifecycles for the whole page session, permanently flagging an address as invalid client-side even in a fresh signup attempt. Initialize the array in init (or set it when the modal opens) instead of on the prototype.

findings.title: action_type is not validated against BlockedEmail.actions
findings.body: The model validates only presence/uniqueness of email. Any integer (or a typo'd value inserted via console/import) is accepted for the NOT NULL action_type column, and should_block? treats every value other than actions[:block] as non-blocking, so a malformed block entry silently fails open instead of surfacing an error. Add an inclusion validation over BlockedEmail.actions.values for action_type.
